title: Heart stent placement
what: Through a small puncture in the wrist or groin, the doctor guides a thin tube to a heart artery. The narrowing is opened with a balloon, and a stent is placed. It is a mesh tube that keeps the artery open.
why: When a heart artery is narrowed and blocks blood flow: for angina and for a heart attack. During a heart attack, it is done urgently.
duration: usually 30 minutes to 2 hours; usually 1 to 3 days in the hospital
tell_doctor: Allergy to iodine or contrast dye
Diabetes and which medicines you take for it
All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will tell you what to stop and when
If you have had bleeding problems

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and often a heart ultrasound. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Before the stent, you are often given anti-clotting medicines. Take them exactly as your doctor said.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for a few hours before the procedure. Your clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Emergency
prepare.text: If you have pressing chest pain right now for more than 15 minutes, do not wait for your appointment. Call emergency services.

bring: A list of all your medicines
Things for 1 to 3 days in the hospital
steps: You lie on the table, an IV is put in a vein, and ECG sensors are stuck on
You are usually given a calming medicine. You stay awake but relaxed
The puncture spot is numbed, at the wrist or groin
A thin tube is guided through the puncture to your heart
Contrast dye is injected and the arteries are viewed on a screen
The narrowing is opened with a balloon and the stent is placed
The tube is removed and a pressure bandage is put on the puncture spot
feel: The numbing shot lasts a couple of seconds. After that, you do not feel the tube
The contrast dye can cause a wave of warmth through your body
When the balloon is inflated, you may briefly feel pressure in your chest. Tell the doctor
after: If the puncture was in the wrist, the bandage stays on for a few hours. Do not strain that arm
If the puncture was in the groin, you usually need to lie flat for a few hours without bending your leg
Drink water. It helps the contrast dye leave your body faster
Do not stop your anti-clotting medicines on your own after a stent. It is dangerous. Your cardiologist will tell you how long to take them
Before any other surgery or tooth removal, tell the doctor about your stent
red_flags: Chest pain, shortness of breath, or cold sweat: call emergency services right away
Bleeding or fast-growing swelling at the puncture spot: press on it and call for help
The arm or leg on the puncture side is cold, pale, or numb
Blood in your urine or stool, or black stool

faq.q: Is a stent placed under general anesthesia?
faq.a: Usually not. The puncture spot is numbed and you get a calming medicine. You stay awake and can talk with the doctor.

faq.q: How long does a stent last?
faq.a: The stent stays in the artery for life. To keep the artery from narrowing again, medicines, not smoking, and controlling blood pressure and cholesterol are important.

reminders.text: Heart stent procedure tomorrow. Bring your ID, test results, and list of medicines. Eat only until the time your clinic gave you.
